That's the only bucket whose default encryption is SSE-S3 (AES256). Caveat: I checked each bucket's default encryption setting only. Objects already stored there keep whatever encryption they were written with, so switching the default to SSE-KMS later will not re-encrypt the existing CSV exports. Also note there is a similarly named 2019 exports bucket; that one already uses a KMS key and is not the one flagged.

1. Listed all buckets in the account (seven).
2. Read the default server-side encryption configuration for each one.
3. Six of them report aws:kms with a KMS key.
4. One reports AES256, which is SSE-S3 with S3-managed keys.
5. That bucket is northwind-legacy-exports.
The bucket still defaulting to SSE-S3 is northwind-data-lake-raw.
Two buckets default to SSE-S3 instead of SSE-KMS: northwind-legacy-exports and northwind-legacy-exports-2019.
